findings.title: Migration crashes unless embed_category exactly matches a category name
findings.body: The migration sets category_id from execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] with no empty-result check. site_settings only stores overridden values, and the default embed_category is a blank string, so a normal install returns zero rows. PG::Result#[] then yields nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate before the fallback. The same unguarded [0] is repeated on line 15 for uncategorized_category_id, so that fallback crashes too if the row is missing. The join also fails (and crashes) when the saved value is a category id, a different case, a renamed category, or blank, even though PostCreator previously accepted that setting. Because this runs for every upgrade, not only embedding sites, the migration cannot be applied as written.

findings.title: Host allowlist is never copied, then the site settings are deleted
findings.body: The import is gated on embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 after a SELECT. PQcmdTuples returns an empty string for SELECT (use ntuples); the pg gem's to_i makes that 0, so the block that copies hosts never runs. Line 31 still deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows. On any database that gets past the category lookup (embed_category equal to a category name), a successful migration therefore drops the existing allowlist and leaves embeddable_hosts empty. Embedding then fails closed for every previously allowed host, and the old values are gone.

findings.title: Copied hosts skip normalization and are interpolated into SQL
findings.body: Even if the import loop runs, each host is inserted with raw SQL and the model callbacks never run. The old allowlist accepted lines like http://eviltrout.com and https://example.com/1234 (the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? stripped the scheme before comparing to URI#host; the new model strips scheme and path in before_validation). record_for_host compares only URI#host (example.com) to the stored string, so those migrated rows never match and existing embeds stop working. The same statement interpolates the host in single quotes (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)). A quote in the value is a syntax error that aborts the migration, or arbitrary SQL if the value is crafted. Use a quoted/bound insert of a normalized hostname (scheme, path, port, whitespace, and case stripped) before deleting the old settings.

findings.title: Host allow-check does not match ports or mixed-case referers
findings.body: host_allowed? / record_for_host decide whether a page may iframe the forum and which category an imported topic uses. The query is lower(host) = ? with the bind value taken from URI#host, which has no port and is not explicitly downcased. before_validation only strips a lowercase http(s):// prefix and a path; it keeps :port and original case, and the format regex explicitly allows a port. Saving example.com:3000 (valid) therefore never matches a referer of http://example.com:3000/..., so the host is denied and TopicEmbed.import gets no category. A mixed-case referer host likewise fails to match a stored example.com because only the column is lowercased. Case variants of the same host can both be stored and .first then picks an arbitrary category.

findings.title: Host regex rejects real hostnames the old setting allowed
findings.body: validates_format_of requires a dotted name whose final label is [a-z]{2,5}. That rejects legitimate embed hosts: TLDs longer than 5 characters (forum.museum, site.photography, and other gTLDs), IPv4 addresses, and localhost. The previous embeddable_hosts setting was a host list compared as hostnames, not this pattern, so those values can no longer be saved from the admin UI and cannot be allow-listed. The same regex's port and path alternatives are misleading: before_validation strips the path but not the port, and a stored port never matches URI#host (see record_for_host).

findings.title: before_validation raises if host is nil
findings.body: The callback calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, which is nil when the key is omitted, then calls save. nil.sub! raises NoMethodError, so the request is a 500 instead of the format validation error render_json_error would have returned for a blank host. Empty string is fine; only nil blows up. The callback also does not downcase, strip whitespace, or remove a port, so values that survive validation still fail host_allowed?.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the host is missing
findings.body: update and destroy load the row with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately use it (save_host(host) / host.destroy) with no nil check. A stale or unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present, so a PUT/POST without that key 500s the same way. The new controller specs never hit these actions.

findings.title: No uniqueness on host, so category assignment is nondeterministic
findings.body: embeddable_hosts.host is not unique, and EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation (the format regex is case-insensitive, so Example.com and example.com are both valid). The admin UI can save the same host twice with different categories. record_for_host uses where(...).first with no ORDER BY, so topic import and the embed allow-check attach an arbitrary category. Add a unique index on lower(host) and a validation that returns a JSON error instead of a duplicate row.

findings.title: Save paints category from the client id, ignoring the server default
findings.body: After host.save resolves, the component sets host.category to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')) and does not use the payload. New rows start with categoryId null, and cantSave only checks the host string, so saving without touching the category chooser is allowed. The server replaces a blank category_id with SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that id. findById(null) does not return the uncategorized category, so the row leaves edit mode with an empty category badge even though a category was stored. The same overwrite drops the badge whenever categoryId does not resolve, which is the default path for the host/category editor this PR adds.

findings.title: Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null
findings.body: The new *_ids branch in _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map without checking that the value is an array. This runs for every rest_serializer payload, not only embeddable hosts. A null embeddable_host_ids (or any other null *_ids key) raises TypeError and rejects store.find / findAll for the parent record. The singular _id branch already no-ops when lookup fails; the plural branch should treat null or a non-array as an empty list instead of throwing.

findings.title: New controller and migration behavior are not tested
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class is a subclass of AdminController. They never POST/PUT/DELETE, so a missing record 500, a nil host 500, invalid hosts, and duplicate hosts are untested. There is no migration spec, so the unguarded embed_category lookup, the cmd_tuples check that skips the copy, and the raw INSERT of scheme-prefixed hosts are not caught. EmbeddableHost specs cover scheme/path trimming on the model but not record_for_host with a port, mixed-case referer, or nil host. The topic expandable_first_post? example titled as failing when no embeddable host exists no longer sets that condition; the method only checks embed_truncate and has_topic_embed?, so the example passes for the wrong reason.
